thread.title: Update: TSX Rises 98 Points as Energy & Cannabis Stocks Advance, Tech Stocks Continue to Slide

title: Update: TSX Rises 98 Points as Energy & Cannabis Stocks Advance, Tech Stocks Continue to Slide
text:
Update: TSX Rises 98 Points as Energy & Cannabis Stocks Advance, Tech Stocks Continue to Slide November 05, 2018, 04:12:15 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Canada's main stock market was in rally mode on Monday, posting a near-triple digit advance. The S&P/TSX Composite Index was up 98 points or 0.65% to close at 15,217. The TSX lost 30 points on Friday. BoC Governor Poloz offered no surprises in a speech today in London, repeating his "rising to neutral" stance on interest rates. U.S. stocks were mixed as investors fretted about U.S.-China trade talks. The Dow Jones gained 190 points while the Nasdaq shed 28 points, weighed by losses in Apple ( AAPL ) shares.
On the TSX, healthcare added 4% as cannabis stocks advanced while energy gained 2% despite flat oil prices . Financials gained 0.3% while tech lost 1.1% and materials were off 0.9% on little changed gold prices .
In stock news, Husky Energy (HSE.TO) gained 2.5% after re-affirming its hostile $6.4 billion bid for MEG Energy. Heavily traded Aurora Cannabis (ACB.TO) rose 2.5% while The Green Organic Dutchman (TGOD.TO) jumped another 26% today after gaining 27% Friday as 100 million free-trading shares became unrestricted, with the 6-month post-IPO lockout window ending. Canopy Growth (WEED.TO) rose 7% today while Baytex Energy (BTE.TO) was up 8%.
In economics news, in a speech in London this morning, BoC Governor Poloz noted the difficulty of reconciling high-frequency financial market action with slower-moving economic fundamentals. He said while it may not always be possible to make sense of the markets, "the effort itself is generally worthwhile." Poloz added that the Bank of Canada must attempt to weigh both upside and downside risks and take a middle, risk-balanced path. "Given our outlook for growth and inflation, the Bank's policy rate will need to rise to a neutral stance to achieve our inflation target," he said, repeating the message he delivered to Parliament and to senators last week.
